messages:
Liam (AE): HarborTech procurement just paused the POC. CFO needs answers to three non-negotiables before exec signoff: 1) live HSM peering with keys never leaving their appliance, 2) private egress peering to their gateway, 3) pilot latency commitment (p95 <= 200ms). Can we triage and confirm who can join an exec bridge tomorrow 9:00am PT?
Tess (SE): Ack. Clarify: do they accept a KMS-proxy that routes signing into their HSM over mTLS, or insist on raw RPC peering?
Liam (AE): They said raw peering is preferred; procurement will accept a documented proxy only if we can prove equivalent crypto controls.
Marco (Presales): Reality: we don't ship direct HSM RPC peering as standard. Short-term options: A) KMS-proxy over mTLS (fast), B) engineering work to enable HSM RPC peering (multi-team effort). For the bridge we should present both with tradeoffs.
Rae (SRE): Ops note: target load ~700 qps, seq=64. Baseline internal numbers for rw-v2-large seq64: p50~50ms p95~130ms. If HSM roundtrip is in-path expect p95 tail to increase. For pilot we recommend Dedicated pool + `--kv-cache` + aggressive batching and a warm canary.
Ivy (Security): Security caveats: live HSM peering raises network and crypto risk. Need vendor FIPS/SOC cert, network diagram, MTLS config, and a completed HSM attestation form. I'll start a risk note and the attestation template.
Dan (Legal): Legal: HSM peering will need a crypto addendum and likely liability carve-outs. Pilot SLAs are possible if timeboxed with limited credits; procurement redlines required.
sys-bot: Ticket HT-42101 created: "HarborTech POC 99 HSM peering + private egress + pilot SLA" assigned to eng-oncall. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/HT-42101
Liam (AE): Can engineering and security commit to attend the bridge at 9:00am PT? We need perf numbers + a short diagram before 8:00am to prep slides.
Rae (SRE): 9:00am PT works for SRE. I'll run a quick mocked-HSM smoke test this evening and post numbers by 7:30am PT. Command: `./smoke_test --model rw-v2-large --concurrency 700 --seq 64 --kv-cache --mock-hsm-latency=25ms`
Tess (SE): I'll prepare two diagrams (direct HSM peering vs KMS-proxy) and a one-page Okta/SCIM checklist (customer asked about SSO too).
Marco (Presales): I'll draft a 3-slide bridge deck: asks, options+tradeoffs, timeline+owners.
Ivy (Security): I'll send the attestation template to their SOC contact and request HSM vendor certs.
Dan (Legal): I'll pre-draft a crypto addendum and a pilot SLA with capped credits. Liam, forward any procurement redlines you have.
Liam (AE): Owners set. If we can get perf numbers and a draft SLA before 7:30am PT we can finalize slides; otherwise escalate to me.
